S1.headline: Nobody at the wheel
S1.body: Kodiak plans unsupervised driverless service on the Dallas to Houston lane by the end of 2026. Aurora said investor day guests could ride part of its route with nobody behind the wheel.
strings: Kodiak plans unsupervised driverless service on the Dallas to Houston lane by the end of 2026. Aurora said investor day guests could ride part of its route with nobody behind the wheel.

S2.headline: 219 miles, Kodiak says
S2.body: That is Kodiak's figure for the Dallas and Houston metros along Interstate 45. Waabi hauls the same corridor and calls it roughly 240.
strings: That is Kodiak's figure for the Dallas and Houston metros along Interstate 45. Waabi hauls the same corridor and calls it roughly 240.

S3.headline: Hands off the wheel
S3.body: A safety observer rides on Kodiak's deliveries from Lancaster to Houston. Kodiak says the observer never touched the wheel.
strings: A safety observer rides on Kodiak's deliveries from Lancaster to Houston. Kodiak says the observer never touched the wheel.

S4.headline: 35 already ran with nobody in the cab
S4.body: Kodiak says 35 driverless trucks were running commercially in its Permian Basin deployment with no humans in the cab at the end of the second quarter.
strings: 35 already ran with nobody in the cab
Kodiak says 35 driverless trucks were running commercially in its Permian Basin deployment with no humans in the cab at the end of the second quarter.

S5.headline: 200 places, 20 trucks
S5.body: Aurora says it is fully allocated to end 2026 with 200 driverless trucks. Breitbart puts the fleet running now at 20. It cites a CNBC ride.
strings: Aurora says it is fully allocated to end 2026 with 200 driverless trucks. Breitbart puts the fleet running now at 20. It cites a CNBC ride.

S6.headline: Six statements and no fee
S6.cite: c1 c5 to c10 c12 ILLUSTRATIVE
S6.body: Since May 28th a company running vehicles with no driver needs a state authorization. The company acknowledges six statements and pays nothing. The authorization does not expire.
strings: Since May 28th a company running vehicles with no driver needs a state authorization. The company acknowledges six statements and pays nothing. The authorization does not expire.

S7.kicker: What the state can't ask for
S7.headline: It carries a recorder
S7.body: The truck must be equipped with a recording device. Dallas asked the state to require crash history too. The department said the statute does not allow it.
strings: The truck must be equipped with a recording device. Dallas asked the state to require crash history too. The department said the statute does not allow it.
What the state can't ask for

S8.headline: The line is serious bodily injury
S8.cite: c13 c15 c16 c17 DRAWN TO SCALE
S8.body: The department counts an operation as endangering the public when it has caused or is likely to cause serious bodily injury. After a final decision an operator has 10 days to ask for a hearing. If it isn't held in time the authorization is reinstated.

S9.headline: A way in
S9.body: A concern about a driverless vehicle that could cause serious bodily injury or death can go to the TxDMV Enforcement Division at txmccs.txdmv.gov/truckstop. Law enforcement can verify authorizations there too.
